extracted.intended_audience: State and Federal Exchange operators, CMS/HHS staff, issuers, agents/brokers/web-brokers, Navigators, and public commenters on the proposed rule
extracted.subtask_description: Preamble to a CMS/HHS proposed rule amending Exchange regulations (evidentiary standards, verification, enrollment timelines, thresholds, and SEPs) with estimates of costs, burdens, and expected impacts; intended to solicit public comment. Useful for stakeholders preparing notice-and-comment responses or implementation planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for Termination for Cause (§ 155.220(g)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Add text to § 155.220(g)(2) to set forth that HHS would apply a 'preponderance of the evidence' standard of proof to assess potential noncompliance under § 155.220(g)(1) and make a determination there was a specific finding or pattern of noncompliance that is sufficiently severe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Codifying the evidentiary standard is intended to improve transparency for agents, brokers, and web-brokers and make the regulations easier to follow; it is not intended to expand the bases for findings of noncompliance or to require more from agents and brokers as part of the enforcement framework. The preamble solicits comment on the impact estimates and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure To File and Reconcile (FTR) change (§ 155.305(f)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend the FTR process to require Exchanges to determine a tax filer ineligible for APTC if HHS notifies the Exchange that the tax filer failed to file a Federal income tax return and reconcile APTC for any year for which tax data would be used to verify APTC eligibility — removing the current flexibility giving tax filers two-consecutive tax years to file and reconcile before removing APTC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conform notice requirements by amending and removing certain notice provisions; expect reduced APTC expenditures (estimates provided: potential Federal APTC savings range $1.16–$1.86 billion annually depending on households affected) but overall impacts are uncertain due to recent system changes and population shifts. Discusses historical rates (18–43% loss of APTC after FTR historically; average 30%); estimates of affected households (approx. 189,000–303,000) and average APTC/month ($548) used to produce savings ranges. Notes appeal rights (consistent with § 155.525) and that enrollees may request continuation of assistance during appeal. Implementation burden estimates: ~10,000 hours per Exchange in 2025 (database/network admin 2,500 hrs @ $101.66; programmer 7,500 hrs @ $95.88); aggregate State Exchanges one-time burden estimated at 200,000 hours costing $19,465,000; Federal one-time burden 10,000 hours costing $973,250; total 210,000 hours at $20,438,250. Seeks comments on burden and less burdensome alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove 60-Day Extension for Income Inconsistency Verification (§ 155.315(f)(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose removing § 155.315(f)(7) which required applicants to receive an automatic 60-day extension in addition to the 90 days currently provided (i.e., reducing the verification window from 150 days to 90 days) to provide documentation to verify DMI including income inconsistencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipated one-time implementation cost to Exchanges of approximately $500,000 each (approx. $9.5 million for 19 State Exchanges). Expect reduction in months of APTC for some households, with estimated numbers losing APTC: ~140,000 on Federal platform and ~86,000 for State Exchanges; using average monthly APTC $588.07 and 2 months reduced yields ~$266 million less APTC expenditures annually. Solicits comments, including whether effect might be smaller if enhanced PTCs expire. Recognizes and requests comment on burdens to State Exchanges and alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Income Verification when Data Sources Indicate Income <100% FPL (DMIs) (§ 155.320(c)(3)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend § 155.320(c)(3)(iii) to create annual income discrepant match indicators (DMIs) when applicants attest to income above 100% of the FPL but trusted data sources show income below 100% of the FPL, requiring additional verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimated increase in annual burden costs: ~$19.7 million for Federal Government and ~$12.1 million total for State Exchanges for document receipt/review/outreach and DMI outcomes; approximate one-time systems update costs: $778,600 Federal and ~$14.8 million for State Exchanges. Consumer burden increase estimated at $13,475,320 annually to submit documentation. Anticipated reduction in APTC recipients: 50,000 (Federal platform) and 31,000 (State Exchanges); estimated APTC reduction ~$189 million annually using four months reduced APTC and $588.07 monthly rate. Also anticipates increased Medicaid enrollment (no quantification) and states verification is minimally burdensome given incentives; seeks comment and data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Income Verification when Tax Data Unavailable (remove § 155.320(c)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose removing § 155.320(c)(5) which requires Exchanges to accept an applicant's income attestation without further verification when tax return data is unavailable, thereby reinstating verification requirements for applicants lacking tax data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimated increases in annual burden costs: ~$76.2 million Federal and ~$46.7 million for State Exchanges for document handling/outreach/DMI determinations; one-time system updates: ~$876,000 Federal and ~$16.6 million for State Exchanges. Consumer annual burden estimated at $52,081,620 to submit documentation. Based on historical DMI and enrollment data, estimate reduction in APTC recipients by 252,000 (Federal platform) and 155,000 (State Exchanges) with estimated annual APTC reduction ~$956 million (using four months reduced APTC and $588.07 monthly). Notes that although it increases burden, it is not expected to deter many eligible people from enrolling; seeks comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual Eligibility Redetermination — $5 Premium for Auto-Reenrolled Fully Subsidized Enrollees (§ 155.335)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend annual redetermination regulation to prevent enrollees from being automatically re-enrolled with APTC that fully covers premium without action; require Exchanges to decrease applied APTC so the enrollee owes $5 for the first month and each following month until they confirm eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FFEs and SBE-FPs must implement starting with benefit year 2026; State Exchanges starting with benefit year 2027. Intent: incentivize enrollees to return to Exchanges to confirm eligibility, improve price sensitivity, better match consumer preferences, reduce improper enrollments and surprise tax liabilities. Acknowledges potential for some coverage terminations for non-payment but expects numbers to be low. Enrollees can update application any time to reinstate full APTC prospectively. Implementation burden estimates: 10,000 hours per Exchange (2,500 hrs database/network admin @ $101.66; 7,500 hrs programmer @ $95.88); aggregate for 20 State Exchanges: 200,000 hours costing $19,465,000; Federal: 10,000 hours costing $973,250; total 210,000 hours at $20,438,250. Exchanges may incur customer service, outreach, and education costs. Discusses expected transfers: likely reduced Federal PTC spending if policies terminate for nonpayment and reduced improper enrollments and commission payments. Requests comments and data where impacts cannot be quantified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic Reenrollment Hierarchy Change — remove bronze-to-silver crosswalk (§ 155.335(j)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose removing § 155.335(j)(4) that allows Exchanges to move a CSR-eligible enrollee from a bronze QHP to a silver QHP in the same product (same provider network and lower or equivalent net premium after APTC), reverting to prior re-enrollment hierarchy standards limiting plan changes on renewal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: retain consumer choice, reduce confusion, reduce risk of accumulating tax liabilities, and reduce switching low-income bronze enrollees into higher-premium silver plans that drive APTC. Anticipates some burdens for Exchanges and CMS to reverse implemented policy (operational and system changes, outreach) but not significant burden for issuers. Expects a small reduction in APTC expenditures; requests comment on impact estimates and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Premium Payment Thresholds — remove fixed-dollar and gross percentage options (§ 155.400(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Modify § 155.400(g) to remove paragraphs allowing issuers to implement fixed dollar and/or gross percentage-based premium payment thresholds (if issuer has not adopted a net percentage-based threshold), leaving only net percentage-based thresholds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: prevent enrollees from remaining enrolled for extended periods without paying any premium and improve program integrity. Notes potential costs for issuers who previously implemented fixed-dollar or gross percentage thresholds to remove or replace those policies. Cites 2026 Payment Notice analysis estimating at-most retention of $817,571,843 in APTC payments by issuers under a fixed-dollar threshold of $10 — which would not occur with removal. Seeks comment on estimates and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual Open Enrollment Period (OEP) change (§ 155.410(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend § 155.410(e) to change the annual OEP for benefit years starting January 1, 2026 and beyond to begin on November 1 and end on December 15 (instead of longer dates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expected benefits: reduce adverse selection, lower premiums and PTC costs, increase continuous coverage, simplify issuer and Exchange operations by eliminating extra month, reduce consumer confusion. Anticipates potential SEP casework increases and temporary consumer outreach costs. Implementation estimates: 4,000 hours per Exchange (1,000 hrs database/network admin @ $101.66; 3,000 hrs programmer @ $95.88); Federal one-time burden 4,000 hours costing $389,300; State Exchanges aggregate 80,000 hours costing $7,786,000; total 84,000 hours at $8,175,300. Does not expect negative impact on enrollment due to system maturity; requests comment on impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeal Monthly SEP for Individuals at ≤150% FPL (§ 155.420(d)(16))
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose removing § 155.420(d)(16) and repealing the 150 percent FPL SEP (and make conforming changes to related regulations), eliminating the SEP that allowed people with projected annual household income ≤150% FPL to enroll year-round.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: expanded availability of fully subsidized plans plus easier access via the 150% FPL SEP opened substantial opportunities for improper enrollments; cites litigation, higher complaints, and sharp enrollment increases among incomes 100–150% FPL in PY 2024 as evidence. Proposes conforming regulatory removals (e.g., §§ 147.104(b)(2)(i)(G), 155.420(a)(4)(ii)(D), 155.420(b)(2)(vii)) and amending § 155.420(a)(4)(iii) introductory text. Seeks comment on impacts and assumptions.
